text:
Cadence

 Live demos · Pragma Research · Documentation · Application demos · Paper · PyPI

 
 

 One continuing equilibrium brain: learn a world, act in it, repair what fails. 

Cadence is a Python library for brains that learn while they live. Animal and human brains learn
from experience and not by backpropagation with gradient descent. Cadence is designed the same
way: its connections change locally while the brain keeps running.

 Install

 

Python 3.11 or later and NumPy. "cadence-net[fast]==0.101.0" adds Numba and SciPy for speed
(recommended); [apple] adds MLX for Apple silicon GPUs and [accel] PyTorch for NVIDIA GPUs.

 A first brain

 

The brain settles: its neurons drive each other until their activity comes to rest, the action
is read from that state, and every synapse learns from the difference between two settles. There
is no backward pass and no switch between training and use.

 Read next, in this order

 Guide What it gives you 
 --- --- --- 
 1 Start here: your first brain the brain above, line by line: settling, lessons and rewards, the state it carries, saving 
 2 Assemble a brain senses by name, a map of things, memories, attention, an ear and a voice, in four whole brains 
 3 Space: tracking what is where a map that keeps things out of view and follows a hidden thing that moves 
 4 Sounds as symbols a sound heard alone brings its thing back, a voice says it, a reward makes it the answer 
 Live demos brains that see, move, play and keep learning, in the browser 
 API reference every public name, with its signature and refusals 

More guides: a continuing life, train a brain, learning from reward,
memory, tune and read a living brain,
backends; the documentation index lists them all. The
released documentation
describes the installed package. Integrated learned world prediction, repair localized to what
failed and cheap stable operation are work in progress; Cadence is alpha research software.

 
 
 
 ▶ Try the brains live: cadence.floatingpragma.ai 

 

 Start with System 1

 Brain.compose builds one association region of 64 neurons between the senses and the motor
choice, and four memories: a working trace, a heard history, a recall memory and an associative
store (the default brain).
Under live the brain learns while young (its first 100 moments) or aroused by an outcome's
surprise or by want, and otherwise answers greedily from one settle; under step it learns from every outcome and from
 teacher= labels. Everything else is opt-in
(assemble a brain).

 live takes the preceding action's measured reward, then chooses the next
action for one continuing stream; supply one observation row per call. It needs
 arousal=True (the founder arousal settings). The working trace advances at every
accepted moment, and so do the recall memory's slots. Tune named settings with compose or brain.retune(...) 
and inspect them with brain.describe() 
(tune and read).
Continuous interaction
covers arousal, resets and saved continuation.

For explicit teaching, batched streams or learning from every outcome, use the
lower-level step loop, which works with or without arousal=True ; its
 teacher= labels the current observation. The
continuing brain example
runs that loop through changed conditions and saved continuation.

A teacher label changes graph parameters. The default associative memory
ignores labels. Add memory choice=True when remembered demonstrations and outcomes should
vote in the choice. Add learned code=units, attention=True when the brain should retrieve a
relevant recent context and its successor, and recall heads=k when one answer needs several
witnessed facts at once. The options can be used together.
Memory
starts with these common cases before giving the complete reference.
A brain trained without a recall memory gets one later: brain.grow(recall=True) , or new output
slots with brain.grow(slots=...) , returns a new brain, the trained one with the part added,
settling as the trained one did until learning gives the part weight. brain.graft(donor, ...) puts trained
regions of another brain into a larger one, such as a trained visual system, or a whole
connectome as one region of a larger anatomy
(grow and combine brains).

 

Imagination carries a private trace without changing live memory, random state
or pending feedback; the composed brain builds no model of the world's
consequences.

Each action solve reports its residual, qualification, sweeps and check counts
in read-only brain.last settlement , as
start a continuing brain
shows. An action whose settle exhausts its budget is refused without changing
live state; qualification and refusal
says when to retry live(observation) without resubmitting the reward.

 

To work from source, install the library repository root as an editable package:

 

 Add optional System 2

 

Observer regions read and return influence to the base, motor regions and earlier
observers. They join the same settlement and use the same interaction interface.
Whether recursive feedback helps on a task is a question for experience and
evaluation.

 How a Cadence brain differs from a feed-forward network

 Brain.compose(inputs=4, actions=2, modules=(64, 32, 16)) builds reciprocal
regions whose activity settles together, so later regions shape earlier ones
while an answer forms, and the action comes from the qualified neural state.
The learner compares local activities in a free and a nudged phase, without a
backward differentiation pass. The relevant comparison with a recurrent
backprop network is acquired behavior and total work on the same task, as
the comparison below
sets out; the contracts
state what each part guarantees.

 Why Cadence

The library puts continuing state, reciprocal interpretation, local plasticity
and memory behind one small interface. A saved brain resumes an action that
awaits its actual outcome, and private imagination inspects responses without
rewriting live experience. These are mechanisms for testing acquisition,
